title: incident-bot: prioritized quicklinks for on-call autodiagnostics
author: Maya Patel
description:
Context: On-call engineers rely on incident-bot autodiagnostics to surface relevant runbooks and tooling during an SLO alert. Currently quicklinks are ordered by static heuristics which often places lower-utility links above high-value runbooks. This PR adds a prioritized quicklinks layer that ranks runbooks and operational links by a small scoring function (SLO relevance, recent usage, runbook freshness, and trust score) to surface higher-value remediation steps first.

What this change does (summary):
- Adds a prioritized quicklinks service that scores candidate links for an alert and returns the top-N to the on-call UI and Slack responses.
- Persists simple usage counters and last-invoked timestamps (TTL-backed) to influence ranking.
- Plumbs scores into the existing incident-bot autodiagnostics response payload; UI displays a priority badge.
- Adds opt-out config and feature flag (incident_bot.features.quicklink_priority) for immediate rollback.
- Adds end-to-end tests for ranking and unit tests for the scoring heuristics.
- Emits telemetry (histogram of chosen-rank, latency for ranking operation, and feature flag percentage) and updates dashboard queries.

Checklist:
- [x] Feature flag guarded
- [x] Unit tests added (scoring, caching)
- [x] E2E test simulating alert -> autodiag -> quicklinks
- [x] Telemetry dashboards updated (Grafana query + alert threshold suggestion)
- [x] Docs: runbook linking behaviour and flag documented in incident-bot README

Commits (high level):
- feat(quicklinks): add prioritized quicklinks service and scoring engine
- feat(config): feature flag and defaults for quicklink priority
- fix(tests): stabilize e2e by mocking time-dependent counters
- ci: add flaky e2e retry for ranking test

Files/areas changed (high level):
- cmd/incident-bot/service/quicklinks.go — scoring engine + TTL cache wrapper
- internal/telemetry/metrics.go — new histograms and counters for ranking selection and latency
- web/ui/src/components/Quicklinks.tsx — show priority badge and trigger tooltip explaining ranking
- docs/runbooks.md — documentation for quicklinks ranking and config flag
- test/e2e/quicklinks_priority_test.go — e2e scenario covering alert -> autodiag -> quicklinks selection
- config/defaults.yaml — feature flag default (off) and cache TTL setting

Rationale: Prioritizing quicklinks reduces mean time to remediation by putting the most actionable runbooks in front of the on-call. We intentionally keep the scoring function small and interpretable to allow quick rollback and tuning. The persisted usage counters are low-cost and TTL-backed to avoid long-lived state. Telemetry allows measuring impact and potential regressions to quicklink utility.

Migration/rollback: The feature is off by default and can be enabled per-org via the feature flag. Removal of the feature flag will fallback to static ordering. No schema migrations required (TTL keys stored in existing redis instance).

Release notes: Adds prioritized quicklinks to incident-bot autodiagnostics (feature-flagged). Improves on-call UX by surfacing higher-value runbooks.

Merge: Squash merge after approvals and CI passed.
